## Engine qualification for the #435 calculations {#wheel-qualification-430}

Engine `8078d7d1` does not qualify to replace the #435 study wheel for round 7. The candidate changes the declared search evidence and misses the #430 objective-reproduction limit in the NaHCO₃ fit. The run used the pinned #435 numerical declarations, starts, weights, bounds and search designs. The fresh cascade was scored separately. The MEA fits consumed the archived salt laws and the receiver fits consumed the archived shared-ion record, so a change in an upstream fitted coefficient did not propagate into the downstream comparisons. [Qualification criteria](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/430) · [Study calculation record](../results/salt-anchored-435/calculation-summary.md)

- The NaHCO₃ objective increased from 0.6067037808541742 to 0.6067037809990378, a relative change of $2.39\times10^{-10}$ against the $10^{-10}$ limit. The largest stage-row osmotic coefficient change was $-1.38\times10^{-11}$ at 278.15 K and 0.01 mol/kg. Both sodium and carbonate intercepts stayed at their lower bound. The Na₂CO₃ slope changed from 0.001963126045030628 to 0.0019631301887990523 K⁻¹.
- The two 307-row MEA replay objectives agreed within $1.51\times10^{-13}$ relative. Each search completed 1,908 grid and 576 offset states with zero descents. The Engine completed every census report, admitted every parent and evaluated all 991,602 supplied trials per endpoint. All 324 census reductions changed from complete to incomplete because Engine #109 added the `dominant-charge-pair-midpoint` optimized seed and the application reducer requires exactly nine optimized trials. The added trial returned no resolved descent in the census. [Engine #109](https://github.com/tannerpolley/epcsaft/commit/1ae2b350f3ac00d48d42abd56a391d6509d76666)
- The normalized 281-row MDEA refit converged at 6.158203731974667 versus 6.16134087650797 on the study wheel. Both used the same starting declaration and weights and retained the same active bounds. The candidate refused trials 2–4 in stage 0 on the Merkley capped-heat row `fit:126` with `saturation:budget_exhausted;saturation:unexamined_gap;`. The study run recorded zero failed trials in that stage. The candidate returned all fitted endpoint predictions. The largest weighted row-cost change came from `fit:125`, where the heat changed from −50.679 to −50.608 kJ/mol.

- DEA retained `start-1` with objective 10.932834014401832 versus 10.932834014387195. Both 1,271-state searches gained the same two available states, `lawson-1976-viii:1:problem` and the 363.15 K, 0.8 mol CO₂/mol DEA, $3P_{\mathrm{bubble}}$ grid state at 13.617310786547122 mol water/mol DEA. Both searches returned zero descents.
- MDEA selected `fit-0` in place of `fit-2`, with objective 537.6587969325753 versus 537.6587969229375. The 11,824-state search gained 142 available entries and lost two. The losses share a bubble failure at 323.15 K, 1.0 mol CO₂/mol MDEA and 3.8899755501222497 mol water/mol MDEA. Its reported row residual was 0.32450 against a $10^{-10}$ limit. All five sampled availability changes reproduced at the exact study parameter point, including both losses. The 75 descent keys and the single confirmed two-liquid split key agreed. Thirteen coexistence attempts changed whether they met the requested tolerance, including the fixed-pressure replay attempts. The fixed-pressure disposition remained unresolved.
- AMP retained both selected fit starts and active bounds. The free and −150 K objectives were 76.31190308635068 and 77.64284261021426, within $1.6\times10^{-13}$ relative of the study endpoints. All four 666-state searches remained available with zero descents. The common-pressure checks retained their physical decisions.
- Part II passed 21 of 23 tests on the candidate and 23 of 23 on the study wheel with `AGENT_HEAVY_CORES=2`. At Hilliard rows 55 and 56, the candidate's charge-pair midpoint seed found liquid witnesses with TPD/RT of −0.03090972724 and −0.04372674105. The tests expected 100 retained witnesses. Each candidate case retained 101.

Unrounded paired results, availability changes, optimizer decisions and phase details are in the [MEA F2](../results/wheel-qualification-430/F2-differences.csv.gz), [MEA F4](../results/wheel-qualification-430/F4-differences.csv.gz) and [other row and state comparisons](../results/wheel-qualification-430/other-differences.csv.gz). The [comparison index](../results/wheel-qualification-430/comparison.json.gz) covers all 69 compared records. It applies the relative objective check away from zero and records changed predictions at returned precision. The [targeted replays](../results/wheel-qualification-430/diagnostics.json.gz) include the two fixed NaHCO₃ parameter points with both wheels. At the archived fit point their cold-replay objectives were 0.606703780949476 and 0.606703780875408, a relative change of $1.22\times10^{-10}$. These are numerical verification results on the declared states and supports.

## Current adoption, 11 November 2026

[#297](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/297) adopts the #255 wide-start primary (`f8f64820…`) on Engine `391dfe5d…`, wheel `0962e21d…`. The [adoption account](../results/adoption-297/README.md) owns the fresh replays, finite stability searches, group rules, conditional information and current numerical package. Observation cost is 148.510545654; the same-wheel outgoing reference costs 148.883260440. Normal default replays cover 153 quantities and all 307 declared observations. This is numerical verification and calibration-quality comparison, not new independent physical validation. MDEA #298, manuscript #259 and delivered review remain separate.

The chronology below retains earlier records and their original evidence. Earlier references to an adopted or reported record describe that study's record; they do not relabel it as the #297 candidate. Generated current tables are identified by their adopted-package inputs.



Historical transfers: 18–19 October 2026 (F1 checks) and 23 October 2026 ([#203](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/203)). The 23 October comparison used the frozen [20 October A7 record](../results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/restricted-2/fit/usable-budget-endpoint.json), `e234e860…`, MEA association volume 0.036287, and its original A6 comparison. Its [transfer account](../results/engine-3e83e19c-adoption/README.md) preserves those identities. The historical #215 record, `00e77608…` at association volume 0.036305439, has separate [one-wheel evidence](../results/engine-3e83e19c-paper-evidence/README.md).

# Question

Did each Engine adoption preserve the numbers it was checked against, and which numerical solver supplied the A7 calculations?

# Result

All three transfers reproduced their compared quantities. The first two checked 152 F1 quantities only. The third, to Engine 3e83e19c, checked every then-current result value reported by the manuscript and changed none of them: all 4,595 compared values are bitwise equal, and the 146 phase-family states of A7 and A6 keep identical classifications and trial outcomes. The only changed values are two seeded split attempts for the A6 comparison fit in supplement Table S10; issue #203 accepted them as disclosed numerical changes. The [current #297 default-path replay](../joint-recalibration/index.qmd#numerical-reproduction) is a separate check.

# Basis and method

Each transfer compares installed merged-commit wheels on the same declared states. F1 is the earlier density-corrected parameter record, not A7. The retained comparison records bind the parameter document, declarations and both wheels.

The 23 October 3e83e19c transfer check reran the existing producers with only their output paths redirected and compared every value by row identity with relative difference $|y_\mathrm{new}-y_\mathrm{old}|/\max(|y_\mathrm{old}|,|y_\mathrm{new}|,10^{-300})$, gate $10^{-10}$ ($10^{-6}$ for the supplement splits). It covers the F1 reference fit's 152 predictions, both 307-row replays (total costs 148.90525398237165 for A7 and 148.23773148349386 for A6), 712 selected-assessment rows and 452 reductions, 2,019 model-curve values, both 73-state phase families, and the A6 seeded splits at states 21, 63 and 70.

# Values

| Engine commits | Quantities compared | Bitwise equal | Worst relative difference (1) | Record |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 84ca269d → 21e761c3 | 152 | 152 | 0 | [Comparison](../results/engine-21e761c3-adoption/comparison.json) |
| 21e761c3 → 8298c602 | 152 | 13 | 2.89e-12 | [Comparison](../results/engine-8298c602-adoption/comparison.json) |
| 8298c602 → 3e83e19c | 4,595 values and 146 phase states | 4,595 values; 146 states identical | 0 | [Check](../results/engine-3e83e19c-adoption/adoption-check.json) |

The 8298c602 transfer covers 152 F1 quantities within 2.9 × 10⁻¹² relative difference. It does not qualify every retained F1 result on that wheel.

The A6 seeded splits were computed on Engine 21e761c3. On 3e83e19c, 101 of their 129 values agree within 3.9 × 10⁻¹⁰, and 28 values change in two attempts:

| A6 state, start | Engine 21e761c3 | Engine 3e83e19c (retained) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 63, water-rich | failed; $\Delta G/(RT)$ −1.3990 × 10⁻⁴ | converged to the same two-liquid state as the uniform start; $\Delta G/(RT)$ −2.1105128438 |
| 21, uniform | failed; $\Delta G/(RT)$ vs original −1.5415 × 10⁻⁵ | still failed; +4.76 × 10⁻⁷ |

Both attempts were already failures on the previous pin, 8298c602. The state-63 change makes the two seeded starts at that state agree. The state-21 values belong to a failed solve and carry no physical meaning. Neither changes a number for the historical A7 parameters, a classification, or a fitted or compared quantity. The `3e83e19c` values are retained for Table S10 ([decision](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/203#issuecomment-6361213910)).

The Engine diff between 8298c602 and 3e83e19c changes no equation, species or phase support, reaction convention or observation operator these declarations select. It changes numerical methods: the stability-polish step limit (the Engine #811 fix), association Newton damping, physical-mole recovery, energy-action caching, and refusal of a phase-amount guess that the old interface ignored. The [adoption record](../results/engine-3e83e19c-adoption/README.md) lists each commit.

# Limits and evidence type

This is numerical verification, not physical validation. The earlier source snapshot was refused on both earlier wheels for its missing ionic-dispersion declaration; it supplies no prediction comparison. The 3e83e19c check does not recompute the conditional standard errors and correlations of either fit, which are local diagnostics of the original fits, or the historical predecessor records; they keep their original Engine provenance.

# Records

The pinned Engine is merged commit `3e83e19ccc771b51d8ebc038931ab25192f4c5b5`, wheel SHA-256 `0d08dff9be39fb8fc9018119c47612f53d823cd0e456914d7dd44c6941596804`, built from that commit with numpy 2.4.4 and scipy 1.17.1. The previous pin was `8298c6029ebb8b467929badc4a223c580ec591ab`, wheel SHA-256 `8897a0caab9f2508ed642f42c8b5226957fbe7035ed7bfdad71e4166798785b3`. No Engine source checkout is imported. The historical A7 results for `e234e860…` were computed on 8298c602 and reproduced bitwise on 3e83e19c in the 23 October transfer; that comparison does not describe the later #212 refits.

Where the historical 20 October A7 calculations called Ipopt, they used the MA57 linear solver; the 3e83e19c wheel also reports MA57. The wheel selects MA57 when the owner's licensed HSL library loads through `EPCSAFT_HSL_LIBRARY`, and MUMPS otherwise (Engine #605). The login environment has set that library since 18 October 2026, and the [A7 launcher](../results/joint-recalibration-170/amendment-7/run.py.txt) passes the inherited environment to every call. The A7 result files do not store the solver; the [8298c602 transfer comparison](../results/engine-8298c602-adoption/comparison.json), run on the same wheel and machine, records `ma57`. The pin before that, 21e761c3, predates that selection and used [MUMPS 5.6](../results/engine-8298c602-adoption/README.md). The Engine reports MA57 and MUMPS states agreeing within about 10⁻¹¹; this repository has not compared the two solvers on A7. Acknowledgement: HSL, a collection of Fortran codes for large-scale scientific computation. <https://www.hsl.rl.ac.uk/>

## Execution record

Transfer commands, timings and installed-wheel checks remain in the linked adoption records. The 3e83e19c check used 15 calls, 238 wall-s and 632 CPU-s at niceness 10 ([checks](../results/engine-3e83e19c-adoption/checks.json)). At that historical transfer commit, pytest passed 95 tests; the four failures were identical on 8298c602 at the base commit.
